conviction_note: Mild long lean: one analyst holds a low Q3 bar ($0.06 EPS on ~$11.6m revenue against $0.10 a year ago and $0.19 last quarter), and the backlog walk in the 17 Nov pre-release points to Q3 revenue at or above that bar. But the backlog and the reaffirmed FY guide are already public, the guide is unlikely to move two weeks after it was reaffirmed, and the slip-to-2027 reading of the same arithmetic cuts the other way. So p_up is 56 on a 6% absolute move, giving +0.72, while the findings sum to +1.8. Most of that gap is the low-EPS-bar finding, which this name has bought before but which is my own inference, not a sourced number.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus: EPS $0.06 and revenue $11.4m-12.0m (single analyst). Chartmill gives $0.06 / $11.598m (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/BOSC/estimates, accessed 2026-11-27); Benzinga gives $0.06 / $11.4m, with Q4 at $0.17 / $15.0m (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/BOSC/earnings-forecasts); Finviz gives EPS next Q of $0.06 (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=BOSC, 2026-11-27). The company guide is FY2026 revenue above $51m and net income above $3.6m, reaffirmed 2026-11-17 (https://finviz.com/news/424062/bos-reports-record-backlog-of-35-million-up-45-from-year-end-2025). The EPS sources agree; revenue sits in a $0.6m range. All of it is effectively one analyst, so sizes are kept modest.
positioning_check: Finviz on 2026-11-27 (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=BOSC): short float 0.14%, short ratio 0.25 days, float 6.53m of 7.06m shares, insiders 8.06%, institutions 19.05%. expectations.real_bar: The backlog ($35m) and the FY floor are already out, so the stock needs Q3 revenue of at least about $12m with EPS clearly above $0.06 and no sign that the FY floor is now a ceiling. A first 2027 frame or an accretive acquisition would be upside.

next_guide.street_full_year: About $52.8m revenue (H1 actual $26.2m + Q3 $11.6m + Q4 $15.0m), derived from the sources above; no published FY figure found
next_guide.company_current_guide: FY2026 revenue above $51m and net income above $3.6m, reaffirmed 2026-11-17 (https://finviz.com/news/424062/bos-reports-record-backlog-of-35-million-up-45-from-year-end-2025)
next_guide.basis: Management reaffirmed rather than raised the FY floors on 17 Nov, with Q3 already closed and two weeks before the print, so a raise on 30 Nov is unlikely. The 2026 outlook was first given with FY results in March, so a formal 2027 guide is unlikely this quarter; the $24m of backlog scheduled for 2027 gives management a qualitative 2027 story.

findings.finding: Q3 EPS consensus of $0.06 (one analyst, ~$11.6m revenue) looks low against the company's own run-rate. Q3 2025 was $0.10 on $11.4m, Q1 2026 $0.11 on $11.4m, Q2 2026 $0.19 on $14.9m. A simple walk on Q2 cost levels (opex about $2.3m a quarter, gross margin 23-25%, financial income $0.2m a quarter from H1's $415k) gives about $0.09-0.10 at consensus revenue. The NI guide (above $3.6m) needs only H2 above $1.5m, against a street H2 of about $1.6m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EPS $0.19 against $0.13 bought +3.5%; Q3 2025 beat-and-raise bought +10.1%; Q1 2026 decline sold -9.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is one analyst's number, and the stock has not run up into the print (20-day +1.1%). If the market expected a beat, the price would have moved toward the $8 target or rallied after the 17 Nov release instead of giving it back by 20 Nov. The cost walk is my own arithmetic, not a published number.
findings.independence: Consensus from https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/BOSC/estimates; Q2 and Q1 actuals from https://finviz.com/news/384037/bos-reports-second-quarter-and-first-half-2026-financial-results and https://finviz.com/news/357681/bos-reports-financial-results-for-the-first-quarter-of-2026. Counterweight: the shekel stayed far stronger year on year (H1 average 3.03 against 3.6 NIS/USD), which may be why the analyst sits low.

findings.finding: The 17 Nov pre-release implies Q3 deliveries from backlog. At 30 Jun about $20m of the $31m backlog was due by year-end; at 30 Sep only $11m of the $35m was due in Q4 and $24m in 2027. So roughly $9m plus the Q4 portion of new Q3 orders (about $1.5-2.5m from the announced 23 Jul, 4 Aug, 10 Aug and 1 Sep orders), minus anything that slipped to 2027, shipped from backlog in Q3. Book-and-ship revenue comes on top. If nothing slipped, that is roughly $12-14m of Q3 revenue against the $11.4-12.0m consensus. Slippage of a few $m would put it below.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue drove both large moves: Q1 2026 revenue fell to $11.4m and the stock dropped -9.7%; Q2 2026 rose +29% to $14.9m and the stock gained +3.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The release gave backlog and delivery buckets but no Q3 revenue, and no aggregator reconciles the two schedules. The stock's +2.7% on the day, given back by 20 Nov, reads as the backlog headline being priced, not a revenue beat.
findings.independence: The 30 Jun schedule comes from a different document, https://finviz.com/news/384037/bos-reports-second-quarter-and-first-half-2026-financial-results. Same 17 Nov document as the backlog and next-guide findings. Caveat (already in the size): the 2027 bucket rose $13m against about $5m of announced 2027-dated orders, which fits either large unannounced orders or deliveries slipping out of 2026.

findings.finding: Record backlog of $35m at 30 Sep 2026 (+45% on $24m at year-end 2025, +13% on $31m at 30 Jun), driven mainly by defense customers, and FY2026 guide reaffirmed, both pre-released on 17 Nov. The $24m due in 2027 equals about 47% of FY2025 revenue, about the cover the $24m year-end 2025 backlog gave 2026 (~50%), so the call has a 2027 growth story to tell.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog-and-guide news moved this name: the Q3 2025 raise on $24m backlog bought +10.1%; this pre-release bought +2.7% on 2026-11-17 (4.15 to 4.26), given back by 20 Nov.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline is mostly priced; it was public 13 days before the print. What is left is how management frames 2027 on the call, which the release did not do.
findings.independence: Defense order flow during the quarter: https://finviz.com/news/387492/bos-secures-23-million-order-from-a-leading-israeli-defense-customer (2026-09-01), https://finviz.com/news/392713/bos-secures-12-million-order-from-a-european-defense-customer (2026-09-16), https://finviz.com/news/417054/bos-robotics-division-secures-650000-order-for-a-robotic-munitions-packing-line-at-a-new-site-of-a-leading-israeli-defense-customer (2026-11-05). Same 17 Nov document as the backlog-walk and next-guide findings.

findings.finding: Next guide: on 17 Nov, with Q3 closed, the company only reaffirmed the FY floors (revenue above $51m, net income above $3.6m). Only $11m of backlog is scheduled for Q4, while the street's Q4 is $15.0m, so the street FY of about $52.8m needs about $4m of Q4 book-and-ship. If management frames FY revenue near $51-52m, the street's Q4 comes down; a raise is unlikely two weeks after a reaffirmation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance direction set the sign on every confirmed print: Q3 2025 raise +10.1%; FY2025 results with a cautious 2026 outlook -10.2%; Q2 2026 NI-guide raise +3.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Q4 consensus ($15.0m, Benzinga) has not been reconciled with the $11m Q4 delivery bucket anywhere public. If it had been, the Q4 estimate would sit nearer $13-14m.
findings.independence: Q4 consensus from https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/BOSC/earnings-forecasts. Same 17 Nov document as the backlog-walk finding, read for a different line (Q4 and FY rather than Q3). Q4 2025 revenue was about $13.0m (FY2025 $51m less H1 $26.6m and Q3 $11.4m), so $15.0m implies +15%.

findings.why_not_priced: This is the description of what is priced: no run-up and no premium, so a clean beat has room. Had the market priced a strong Q3, the stock would be above its 17-18 Nov level of 4.26-4.35 by more than the 2% it is.

findings.finding: The shekel weakened about 2.9% against the dollar over Q3 2026 (Bank of Israel, 3 Nov), after strengthening 5.9% in Q2. That eases the NIS-cost opex pressure quarter on quarter (the CFO put the H1 hit at $0.6m). Year on year it is still a headwind: the H1 2026 average was 3.03 NIS/USD against 3.6, and the Q3 2025 average was 3.36.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The currency was cited as the drag in the Q1 2026 release (-9.7%) and offset in Q2 (+3.5%); never the stated driver of a move on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: A one-analyst model is unlikely to have re-marked Q3 opex for an intra-quarter currency reversal. The effect is small and partly offset by unknown FX effects in financial income.
findings.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed for Q3. The company's own H1 currency figures are at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1005516/000121390026104997/ea030688101ex99-2.htm.

findings.finding: M&A: on the Q2 call (20 Aug) management said it was in negotiations with several targets (EBITDA multiple 5-6x, up to $20m with about 50% bank financing), with $2.9m of exercise proceeds earmarked. An accretive deal could be announced with the results.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No acquisition announcements in the reaction history.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing has been announced in three months, so the market assigns little probability to it. If a deal were expected, the stock would show a premium over its post-17 Nov level.
findings.independence: The H1 MD&A repeats the earmarking: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1005516/000121390026104997/ea030688101ex99-2.htm

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CEO said he expects higher gross margins from price increases made since the start of the year, but warned that large supply-chain deals ($1.5-2m) carry lower margin. Q2 gross margin was 23.0% against 24.9% in Q1 and 24.9% in Q3 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin has not been the stated driver of a print move.
findings.why_not_priced: A low $0.06 EPS bar implies no margin recovery is modelled. Q3's mix toward defense robotics and supply-chain deliveries is unknown, so the direction is uncertain.

baseline_tension: There is no skew (no options market) and only a flat 20-day run-up, so the evidence does not fight a priced lean. The main tension is internal: the same 17 Nov backlog walk supports a Q3 revenue beat if nothing slipped and a miss if deliveries moved to 2027.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (documents beat inference): the EPS-bar finding rests on my own cost walk, not a published figure, so cut from +1.0 to +0.8.
Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the backlog-walk finding's slippage caveat is unresolved, so cut from +0.5 to +0.3, and print_vs_bar_pct cut from +6 to +4.
Rule 5 (proxy and transmission): the shekel macro finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1; the Elbit counterparty finding has no stated link, cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): EPS $0.06 agrees across Chartmill, Benzinga and Finviz, but it is one analyst, so sizes stay small; no hard cap applied.

Reaction history from the wrong events: confirmed-print reactions (+10.1, -10.2, -9.7, +3.5) used for abs_move_pct, not the baseline's 2.61. abs_move held at 6 because the backlog was pre-released. Rule 8 does not raise it, since none of my findings is a confirmed unpriced number.
